newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Cricket-Caribbean mission tests Indian resolve.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-Caribbean mission tests Indian resolve.

text.p: Sachin Tendulkar resumes his unavoidable batting rivalry with Brian Lara at Sabina Park on Thursday at the start of a five-test series between India and West Indies he believes will be a trial of stamina as much as skill.

The Indian captain, bidding to improve his side's poor recent test away record in the unforgiving environment of the Caribbean where India have won just a solitary test series in 44 years, is doing his best to deflect suggestions of a personal duel with Lara.

His more immediate priority is to find a way of lifting an Indian team who will have been on international cricket's remorseless treadmill almost non-stop for 12 months by the time they fly home in May.

"It's been one long trek," said Tendulkar, still only 23 but already a veteran of seven years on the international scene. "We went to England, then we went to Sri Lanka and Canada, then Australia came to India, we played a triangular one-day series, then we had a test series against South Africa, then we played a test series in South Africa and one-day games in South Africa and Zimbabwe."

Apart from a superb 169 against South Africa in Cape Town, Tendulkar has managed only one other fifty in his last 14 test innings and has slipped to 10th in the latest Coopers and Lybrand world batting ratings.

He admitted in an interview with the Jamaica Gleaner on Tuesday he was feeling the strain, and acknowledged a full-length series against West Indies would allow the team scant chance to recharge their batteries.
"It is not going to be an easy task playing the West Indies in the West Indies. Basically we want to go out, play good cricket that people will enjoy and give it our all."

The form of Steve Waugh has widened the debate on who should be considered the world's best batsmen, but this forthcoming series gives both Tendulkar and Lara the chance to underline their value to their respective sides.

Lara, who averages 56.33 in 38 tests against Tendulkar's 49.67 in 48, failed to make the impact he would have wished in West Indies' 3-2 series defeat in Australia, but must be fancied to improve his figures against an injury-hit Indian bowling attack.

Javagal Srinath's shoulder injury puts a huge responsibility on his regular opening partner Venkatesh Prasad and leg-spinner Anil Kumble, and Tendulkar is looking to himself and Mohammad Azharuddin to ease the pressure with some big runs.
"I think Azhar has been absolutely marvellous and he has a responsibility out there being the senior-most member of the side.
"The players and the people expect a lot of things from him which I know he is capable of doing. I just hope he gets runs on this tour.

India's only series win in the Caribbean was under Ajit Wadekar in 1970-71, but Tendulkar's men can at least point to their one-off test win over Australia in Delhi in October followed by a home series win over South Africa as evidence they should not be considered pushovers.

West Indies (from) - Stuart Williams, Sherwin Campbell, Shivnarine Chanderpaul, Brian Lara, Carl Hooper, Jimmy Adams, Roland Holder, Junior Murray, Curtly Ambrose, Ian Bishop, Courtney Walsh, (captain), Rawl Lewis, Franklyn Rose.

India (from) - Navjot Sidhu, Nayan Mongia, Saurav Ganguly, Sachin Tendulkar (captain), Rahul Dravid, Mohammad Azharuddin, Vangipurappu Laxman, Ajay Jadeja, Venkatesh Prasad, Anil Kumble, Sunil Joshi, Dodanarsiah Ganesh, Robin Singh, Saba Karim, Abey Kuruvilla.
